articles.title: Trump under pressure on Iran war after Republicans' midterms defeat
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump concedes that the war he ordered on Iran was partly to blame for his Republican Party's sweeping midterms losses -- but even as he comes under pressure, analysts said Wednesday that he has few good options ahead. It remains to be seen what path Trump will take after emerging politically weakened as Democrats seized control of both the Senate and House of Representatives in Tuesday's vote.

articles.title: US lawmakers will go to UN climate talks in Turkey
articles.summary: An American congressional delegation will travel to Turkey for the annual UN climate summit, a Democratic lawmaker said Wednesday, a day after his party's landslide midterm victory. The United States is not taking part in the negotiations after President Donald Trump withdrew the country from the Paris agreement for a second time upon returning to office. But Representative Sean Casten of Illinois said the 19-member delegation would nevertheless play an "important diplomatic function" at COP31 which runs from November 9 to 20 in Antalya.

articles.title: US slaps sanctions on Indian, Turkish firms and people for aiding Iran

The sanctions are part of the Trump administration's "Operation Economic Outcast," which aims to cut off Iran's ability to sell oil to fund the war with the United States.

"The Iran thing we had to do, and we continue to do it," he told reporters. The Iran war was responsible for a spike in gasoline prices that were seen as a strong factor in why Democrats made big gains in the elections. Trump said the war has been worth it to stop Tehran from "having a nuclear weapon."

articles.title: Analysis-Beaten at home, Trump faces stark choice on Iran: deal or escalation
articles.summary: By Samia Nakhoul DUBAI, Nov 4 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump went to war seeking regime change in Iran. Instead, it was his own grip on Washington that gave way, as voters weary of the war and hit by soaring fuel prices handed Democrats control of Congress. That leaves a weakened president facing a choice between a negotiated exit and a riskier escalation. In Tehran and among its allies, the result was swiftly cast as a verdict on the conflict. Across the Gulf, officials were left wondering which way Trump would turn.
